A1.justification: Both readable, ten-page PDFs describe the same ReNeg work and support direct comparison of the supplied text, equations, figures and tables. Neither contains an appendix, despite appendix references in Sections 4.1 and 5.4; those referenced materials cannot be assessed.

before.justification: v1 reports original parameter-efficiency measurements, image-generation benchmarks and transfer experiments involving ControlNet and video-generation models in Tables 1–5 and Figures 3–7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including HPSv2 and Parti-Prompts evaluations and image/video transfer experiments.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same reward-guided embedding optimization, CFG training, DDIM sampling and per-sample adaptation procedure.

E1.justification: Both use ImageReward training prompts, HPSv2 and Parti-Prompts evaluation, and the same image-generation, ControlNet pose-to-image and video-generation scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same direct-inference, prompt-refinement and model-finetuning comparators, including Diffusion-DPO and TextCraftor (Text). Figure 5 retains its separate comparator set, including DPO-Diff. Transfer comparisons are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the same sample counts, metrics and settings: 4,000 training steps, batch size 64, learning rate 0.005, and 30-step DDIM inference with guidance 7.5 at 512 × 512 resolution.

E4.justification: Both contain the same parameter-efficiency pilot study, DDIM-versus-DDPM analysis, global-versus-per-sample comparison, negative-embedding visualizations and generalization analyses. No analysis is added or removed from the supplied PDFs.

E5.justification: Figure 5 retains the statement that comparisons use the same initial noise and seed. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported numerical and qualitative results match. For example, Table 2 retains Parti-Prompts HPSv2.1 scores of 29.16 and 29.84 for global and per-sample embeddings, respectively. Tables 1 and 3–5 and the plotted findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, the Jacobian-based parameter-efficiency definition in Section 4.1 and the accompanying mathematical reasoning are unchanged. Neither supplied PDF contains the referenced appendix details.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about learning global and per-sample negative embeddings, improving preference alignment and transferring embeddings across models sharing a text encoder.

C2.justification: Both retain the same efficiency rationale, embedding interpretations and transfer conditions. The conclusion still acknowledges semantic deviations caused by limitations of the base generative model.

D1.justification: v2 adds an abstract sentence announcing released code and learned negative embeddings; v1 has no corresponding announcement. However, the new 'this URL' annotation is encoded as an internal jump to page 1, not a working external repository link. Implementation details otherwise match.

R1.justification: The same 41 references and related-work comparisons are retained. The positioning relative to discrete prompt optimization, prompt refinement and diffusion-model finetuning is unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract gains the resource-release sentence and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. Body wording, terminology and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added sentence causes minor text reflow across pages 1–5 and adjusts spacing around Algorithm 1. All seven figures and five tables retain their content and design; pages 6–10 render identically.

improvement.justification: The scientific argument, experimental evidence and limitations are unchanged. The added resource-release notice has limited practical value because its link resolves internally to page 1. Together with minor text reflow and version metadata changes, this produces no meaningful overall quality difference in the supplied PDFs.
